$comment: Recipe for the recorded half of assets/sfx: excerpts cut from the #GameAudioGDC bundle the operator holds locally (royalty-free, commercial use, modification permitted, no attribution required). Selection rationale and the taxonomy these ids fill are in docs/research/2026-09-07-video-sfx-and-ambience-library.md; the ids are the same ones the generated recipe defines, because the point of this file is to put a real recording behind an id wherever the bundle holds one that is better than a generation. 27 ids here replace a generated sound of the same name and 11 are new. What is deliberately NOT here: every id the bundle cannot serve honestly. There is no stream in it, no night-only cricket bed, and its nearest office room tone is a fridge; those three stay generated rather than be filled with something that is nearly the sound. A ticking-clock BED was cut for the same reason and then dropped: a metronomic event inside a loop announces the wrap on every cycle, which is exactly what qc.event_prominence_db exists to catch, so the clock is here as a single tick instead. No timestamps are written by hand. Beds name a length and the builder sweeps the whole recording for the evenest window of it; one-shots name which event they want and the builder gates the file to find it.
